encoding/binary#

Explicit fixed-width numeric binary representations.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let network is @byte = IntegerBytes(
    value: -2,
    size: 2,
    signedness: Signedness.signed,
    order: ByteOrder.big,
).bytes(); // [255, 254]

let measurement is float = Binary(
    bytes: [byte(64), byte(32), byte(0), byte(0)],
    order: ByteOrder.big,
).float(FloatWidth.bits32); // 2.5
let port is int = Binary(bytes: header, order: ByteOrder.big).int(Signedness.unsigned);

Description#

Explicit fixed-width numeric binary representations.

Signed integers use two's complement; unsigned integers use ordinary magnitude. Encoding is exact and never truncates, wraps or saturates. Decoding must fit Okkama's signed 64-bit int, although redundant leading zero or sign-extension bytes are accepted. Integer widths are positive.

Floats use IEEE 754 binary32 or binary64 with explicit byte order. binary32 encoding rounds to nearest with ties to even. Okkama floats are finite, so decoding an infinity or NaN is rejected. Signed zero and subnormal values retain their IEEE representation. No API uses machine-native byte order.

A generic BinaryLayout/Packed/Unpacked layer is intentionally absent. Until the language has typed heterogeneous product values, such an API would need either an untyped value bag or a string format DSL. Callers compose these typed scalar representations into protocol-specific objects instead.
